proposal.explanation: Fixed deadlocks in the non-keep-enabled width adapter paths (upsizing and downsizing) by replacing fragile two-flop state machines with robust beat-counter based skid-buffer handshakes. The upsizing path now uses a `read_count` counter to buffer input beats, asserting `output_axis_tvalid` only when a full output word is assembled and `output_axis_tready` is high, while `input_axis_tready` tracks output buffer availability. The downsizing path uses a `write_count` counter to shift out beats from a buffered input word, asserting `input_axis_tready` when the buffer is empty or the output accepts a beat. TUSER/TID/TDEST/TKEEP signals are captured on the first input beat (upsizing) or first output beat (downsizing) for frame alignment. The keep-enabled submodules (`axis_data_width_adapter_input_keep`, `axis_data_width_adapter_output_keep`, `axis_data_width_adapter_passthrough`, `axis_skid_buffer`) are retained and cleaned up with SystemVerilog syntax as they passed validation.

review.error: Keep the template license, module parameters and ports byte-identical
review.limitation: Directed simulations plus bounded two-state comparison to a historical reference; no unbounded proof or coverage of all parameters. Fixed references are excluded from model prompts.
review.scope: S_KEEP_ENABLE=0 means every source byte is valid regardless of s_axis_tkeep. Preserve frames, byte validity and ID/DEST/USER across 8-to-8/16/32-bit paths and stalls, including enabled source masks.
